name: Java
summary: Statically typed, class-based, garbage-collected language compiled to JVM bytecode. It is defined by two vendor specifications maintained through the Java Community Process and OpenJDK: the Java Language Specification (source language) and the Java Virtual Machine Specification (class files and execution).

level_notes.0: OpenJDK (openjdk/jdk) is the reference implementation: javac lives in src/jdk.compiler, the HotSpot VM in src/hotspot and the class library in src/java.base. Independent implementations include the Eclipse compiler (ECJ), Eclipse OpenJ9 and GraalVM. The TCK (JCK) that decides conformance is not open source; jtreg tests in the OpenJDK tree are the public stand-in.
level_notes.1: No ISO/ECMA standard. The JLS and JVMS (one edition per Java SE release, produced by a JSR) are normative; language changes arrive as JEPs, often first as preview features (JEP 12). The Java SE API specification is the third normative part of a Java SE platform release.
level_notes.2: Oracle's dev.java tutorials supersede the older 'Java Tutorials' (frozen at JDK 8) which are still widely cited.
